Subject: Embeddings integration: vector dims, batching, migration - next steps

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — great conversation and clear priorities. Quick recap + proposed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Recap
- Current stack: you're using VendorX embeddings (1536-dim) for semantic search + a lightweight reranker on top.
- Primary goals: reduce per-query cost while keeping search quality, improve bulk reindex time for frequent product updates, and get predictable latency for customer-facing queries.

Technical notes we discussed
- Vector dims: VendorX uses 1536; we suggested benchmarking 1024 vs 1536 with our curated models (tradeoff: lower dims = lower storage & compute, may slightly affect accuracy depending on corpus).
- Normalization: L2 normalization before storing vectors + cosine similarity at query time is recommended for cross-model consistency.
- Batching: aim for batch sizes 64-256 depending on your latency SLO; we can auto-batch in the SDK or run bulk jobs on Dedicated capacity.
- Migration pattern: export existing vectors -> re-embed new vectors (chunked bulk jobs) -> versioned index swap (zero-downtime).

Attachments: I've attached a short migration plan and a sample batching CSV for your infra team to preview.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with Dev (we've CC'd Dev) to lock in API/SDK auth, preferred model, and batching strategy (30-45m).
2) Share a small sample dataset (1-2k docs) so we can run a quick quality & cost benchmark.
3) We'll produce a migration timeline and cost estimate (PO/SOW as needed).

Can you confirm which times next week work for the deep-dive? Also confirm whether you'd prefer we benchmark 1024 or 1536 dims first (or both).

Thanks —

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Dimension: VendorX is currently at 1536. Our internal QA has historically seen marginal regressions when dropping below 1536 on certain query types (product title fuzziness). Happy to run 1024 vs 1536 but can you add guidance on expected delta in recall?
- Batching: our current bulk job runs at ~10k docs/hour using their managed endpoint. We'd like to know expected throughput on Redwood Dedicated for a comparable instance type (gpus per worker) so we can plan windows.
- Normalization: we're onboarded to cosine today; our vector store supports both normalized vectors and raw euclidean distances. In your migration plan, do you prefer storing normalized vectors or storing raw and normalizing at query time?

I've attached a small metrics export for the bulk job.

Hi Samir / Priya —

Following up with the technical detail we discussed. I'll run a quick internal benchmark once you share the 1-2k sample, but below are recommendations and what to expect.

Auth & SDK:
- Use the Redwood SDK (Python/node) for bulk and streaming embeddings. Auth via API key (short-lived keys + KMS integration available for Private). Example: redwood.client = Redwood(api_key=...)
- Routing: for production queries, route to our embeddings endpoint (POST /v1/embeddings) with the model param; for backfill jobs use the bulk import endpoint with chunking.

Vector dims & models:
- Recommended approach: A/B benchmark 1024 and 1536 using a representative sample set. If your queries involve short titles + brand tokens, 1536 tends to preserve subtle lexical distinctions better. For long-document semantic similarity, 1024 often matches quality with much lower storage.
- Model selection: we can provide two candidate models tuned for retrieval: rwd-embed-1024-v1 and rwd-embed-1536-v1. Both are quantization-friendly and support cosine at query-time.

Normalization & similarity:
- Store L2-normalized vectors in your vector DB (recommended). Storing normalized vectors means you can use dot-product as cosine directly and reduce per-query computation. If you cannot normalize on write, normalize at query time but expect slightly higher CPU at query.

Batching & throughput:
- Bulk reindex: use chunk sizes of 2k-10k docs per worker job depending on memory and GPU allocation; smaller chunks reduce memory spikes.
- Real-time embedding: client-side batching 64-256 is a good starting point. For Dedicated GPUs with 8xA10 equivalent, expect ~200-600 embeddings/sec at 1536 dims (model-dependent).

Migration pattern (zero-downtime):
1) Export existing vectors + metadata (id, text, old_vector)
2) Run parallel embedding job to generate new vectors (version-tag them: embed_v2) -> store in staging index
3) Run A/B traffic split & reranker validation on a subset (we can help with eval scripts)
4) Swap index once QA pass complete -> retire old vectors after a rollback window

Reranker guidance:
- Use a lightweight cross-encoder reranker only for top-K candidate rescoring (K=10-50). This keeps cost low while improving precision.

Attachments: sample CSV looks good. I've attached a small sample-embeddings-batch.csv template you can use for the backfill.

I'll run a quick throughput benchmark when you share the sample and confirm GPU profile you're planning to use.

- Dev
